Maya G: heads-up — FP8 canary showed a repeat/collapse pattern in a 4k convo around token ~2000, saving logs here
Jordan K: ah ok, repro steps?
Maya G: ran:
```
rdw canary-run --model redwood-mid-fp8 --prompt-file tests/long_convo_v2.json --seq-len 4096 --seed 7
```
Maya G: trimmed logs:
```
2025-06-02T11:03:12Z token=1998 prob_drop=0.88 rep_window=36
2025-06-02T11:03:12Z token=1999 top1_score=0.994 -> repeated fragment
2025-06-02T11:03:12Z kv_cache_hit=0.08 quant_scale=3.5
```
Liam P: smells like per-head scale blowup + kv cache reuse. fp8 calibration probably missing tail outliers for longctx.
Priya S: can we detect at runtime and route to an alternate precision? per-token entropy or a simple degscore spike could work.
Jordan K: two quick ideas:
- cheap: rolling entropy drop < 0.5 over 5 tokens -> fallback to INT8
- robust: track per-request deg_score, if >0.7 switch to FP16 for rest of request
Maya G: agree on both. fallback cost ~2x but keeps correctness. need per-customer opt-in and SLA flags.
Liam P: also propose a canary-only sampler that records kv scales + head-wise norms + a short window of tokens for offline analysis. metric name: fp8_longctx_incidents.
SRE-Bot: note: enabling automatic fallback will increase GPU time/cost. Recommend a cost guard and alert if fallback rate > 1% for prod.
Maya G: action items:
- Jordan -> add sampler + dashboard tile for canary (include sampled payloads)
- Liam -> implement rolling-entropy detector + per-request fallback hook (feature flagged)
- Priya -> add per-tenant SLA knob and fallback budget in config
- Ops -> run extended canary with sampling for 72h, mute noisy canary alerts
Jordan K: I'll add dashboard + alert that fires if fp8_longctx_incidents > 3% of canary traffic.
Maya G: opened ticket RDW-4281 (fp8-longctx-repro). will post canary results there and attach sampled traces.
Priya S: short-term mitigation: cold-start kv cache for long-context workloads and increase calibration samples for tail tokens.
Liam P: noted. After canary, we should evaluate fallback latency overhead and iterate on detection thresholds.
Maya G: thanks all — tagging @SRE-Bot and @billing to watch cost during extended canary :eyes:
